lede: Which forecasting models work on real energy data? Load, solar, wind, power prices and fuel markets, scored with one protocol across statistical baselines, trained deep networks and zero-shot foundation models.

slices.label: Fresh track (post-2025-10 test data)
slices.note: Test data from 2025-10 onward, after the evaluated foundation models' training data was collected.

slices.label: Classic research datasets
slices.note: Several classic datasets are inside foundation-model pre-training corpora; compare with the Fresh slice.

method: Fresh track: live public feeds from system operators, power exchanges and statistical agencies, with a test period from 1 October 2025 to 30 September 2026, after the training cut-off of the evaluated foundation models. Classic track: datasets established in the literature, with the final 20 % of each series as the test split.

Two horizons per dataset, matched to operational use: day- and week-ahead for hourly and sub-hourly data, 5 and 20 trading days for daily prices, 4 and 13 weeks for weekly data, and 3 and 12 months for monthly data.
Up to 60 non-overlapping origins per task, identical for all models and series. Panels with more than 100 series are scored on a fixed random subset of 100 series.

Foundation models are applied zero-shot with up to 2,048 context values. Deep models from the Time-Series-Library are trained per task and early-stopped on a validation split. Statistical models are re-estimated at every origin.

Probabilistic accuracy is measured by the weighted quantile loss (WQL) over the 0.1–0.9 quantiles and point accuracy by the mean absolute scaled error (MASE) of the median. For point forecasters WQL reduces to WAPE.

Task scores are normalised by those of Seasonal Naive and aggregated by the geometric mean, with average ranks reported alongside. A model is ranked on a slice only when all of its tasks are complete.
attribution: Data: EIA (public domain), Energy-Charts/Fraunhofer ISE & SMARD (CC BY 4.0), AEMO, NESO, Sheffield Solar PV_Live, NYISO, ONS, ODRÉ, Energinet, NZ Electricity Authority, Elexon, World Bank, and the research datasets listed above under their own licences. Datasets in evaluation: JEPX and the Japanese transmission system operators, KPX (Korea), IESO (Ontario), CAISO, CENACE (Mexico), XM (Colombia; consulted in Sinergox de XM S.A. E.S.P.), COES (Peru), ADME (Uruguay), CAMMESA (Argentina) and AEMO (Western Australia).
method_note: Excluded models: Moirai-MoE 1.0, owing to the inference cost of autoregressive sampling at horizons of 336–1,008 steps, and TimeH2O, whose weights are gated.
